entry.title: Watch a hand’s shadow
entry.invitation: Make a hand shadow and see what catches their eye.
entry.summary: Hold your hand with light behind it and let its shadow offer something for your baby to notice.
entry.cue: Your baby is awake, comfortable and interested in looking.
detail: The authors include hand shadows among the simple things a young baby can watch. Notice where their gaze settles and give them time to look.

They also describe light and shadow moving through leaves and branches, or a high-contrast picture within the baby’s view. Follow the interest you see; looking away or becoming upset is a reason to stop or change what is offered.

ageContext.readiness: Awake, comfortable interest in watching light, shadow or movement.
ageContext.note: Follow the interest you see, without a set looking time.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
